title: Welton probe complete, inquest looms
article: On the eve of a coroner's inquest into the police shooting death of Derek Welton, an RCMP spokesperson has confirmed police investigation into the matter is over.
Cpl. Darren Lagan said an investigation conducted by the Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit, which includes municipal and RCMP officers, is done.
But he refused to comment on anything else to do with the case, including when the investigation concluded.
"I'm not going to comment on it. I won't comment before the inquest. It would be inappropriate."
Instead, he referred questions to Grant Hamilton of the Victoria Police Deapertment, who was unavailable by press time Thursday.
Meanwhile, the B.C. Coroners Service inquest into the police-involved death begins Monday.
Welton, 39, was shot and killed by a member of the North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP on March 1, 2009.
Now presiding coroner Rodrick MacKenzie and a jury will publicly hear evidence from subpoenaed witnesses to determine the facts surrounding Welton's death.
As reported previously, five officers arrived at the Duncan R.V. Park & Campground at about 6 p.m. the night Welton died, responding to an abandoned 911 call.
At some point, Welton armed himself with a knife, and police said they utilized multiple force options, including use of a Taser, without success.
A senior officer with 11 years on the job fired his weapon and hit Welton. Police did not say how many rounds were fired or where Welton was hit.
Inquests into police-involved deaths are typically automatic.
Welton's starts on Jan. 31 at the Duncan Law Courts.
